scope: Selective foundational digital-twin, urban integration, credibility and XR evidence; not exhaustive. IDs T01-T12.

sources.citation: Kritzinger, W., Karner, M., Traar, G., Henjes, J., & Sihn, W. (2018). Digital Twin in manufacturing: A categorical literature review and classification. IFAC-PapersOnLine, 51(11), 1016-1022.
sources.question: How can manufacturing literature be categorized by integration?
sources.data: Literature corpus; counts not checked in full text.
sources.evaluation: Classification, not an empirical system benchmark.
sources.supported_finding: An influential integration taxonomy distinguishes digital models, shadows and twins; the abstract reports less literature at its highest integration level.
sources.limitations: Manufacturing-specific and historical; not a universal definition or evidence of present scarcity.
sources.reproducibility_access: Publisher indexed abstract verified; direct page fetch returned 403. No full-text method claims.
sources.relevance: Vocabulary baseline, to be compared with T02/T03/T11.

sources.citation: Jones, D., Snider, C., Nassehi, A., Yon, J., & Hicks, B. (2020). Characterising the Digital Twin: A systematic literature review. CIRP Journal of Manufacturing Science and Technology, 29, 36-52.
sources.type: Peer-reviewed systematic review; author accepted manuscript read
sources.question: Which concepts and processes recur across twin descriptions?
sources.method: Google Scholar first 500 results plus citation expansion; thematic analysis.
sources.evaluation: Theme mapping; no operational accuracy benchmark.
sources.supported_finding: Separates entity, environment, state, measurement, realization and synchronization rate. Discusses one-way definitions despite original bidirectional framing.
sources.limitations: Manufacturing-heavy corpus; search horizon predates recent urban/neural work.
sources.reproducibility_access: Open CC BY accepted manuscript retained locally; corpus methodology described.
sources.reading_depth: Deep anchor: section 2, sections 3.1.5-3.1.13; manuscript pp.4-7,11-17; Fig.5 visually inspected (PDF page14).
sources.relevance: Specify what is measured, what changes and at what rate, rather than calling a renderer a twin.

sources.citation: Glaessgen, E. H., & Stargel, D. S. (2012). The Digital Twin Paradigm for Future NASA and U.S. Air Force Vehicles. 53rd AIAA/ASME/ASCE/AHS/ASC Structures, Structural Dynamics and Materials Conference, AIAA 2012-1818.
sources.question: How could asset-specific models improve future vehicle sustainment?
sources.method: Conceptual synthesis of physical models, onboard sensing and lifecycle records.
sources.data: Illustrative aerospace cases; no integrated-twin trial dataset.
sources.evaluation: Discusses conventional practice and future capabilities; not a controlled comparative trial.
sources.supported_finding: Defines a probabilistic multiphysics, multiscale asset-specific simulation informed by sensor and fleet history.
sources.limitations: Aspirational aerospace framing; projected reliability gains are not demonstrated results.
sources.reproducibility_access: NASA public PDF accessible; no runnable integrated implementation established.
sources.reading_depth: Targeted full text: Concept and Attributes, pp.6-10; introduction and summary.
sources.relevance: Shows why the physical/data relationship and prediction matter beyond visualization.

sources.citation: Kapteyn, M. G., Pretorius, J. V. R., & Willcox, K. E. (2021). A probabilistic graphical model foundation for enabling predictive digital twins at scale. Nature Computational Science, 1, 337-347.
sources.type: Peer-reviewed methods and experimental/simulation paper; author manuscript read
sources.question: How can calibration, estimation, prediction and decisions share an uncertainty-aware formulation?
sources.method: Probabilistic graphical model and Bayesian updating of a UAV structural model.
sources.data: Physical wing geometry, load-displacement and dynamic response calibration; simulated operational mission and noisy strain observations.
sources.evaluation: Prior/posterior calibration; modal discrepancy; normalized strain prediction error; estimated versus prescribed structural-health evolution and control switching.
sources.supported_finding: Demonstrates unified calibration and simulated health-aware operation; Fig.6 distinguishes estimation from future prediction and exposes unequal parameter uncertainty.
sources.limitations: Operational demonstration is simulated, not validated fleet deployment; model discrepancy and observability remain challenges.
sources.reproducibility_access: Paper reports public calibration and simulation repositories, but proprietary Akselos solver; model-output data supplied instead. Repositories not run.
sources.reading_depth: Deep anchor: formulation, calibration/operational results pp.3-9, calibration methods pp.10-12, availability p.15; Fig.6 visually inspected.
sources.relevance: Concrete example of uncertainty propagation and explicit held-future prediction, transferable as principles rather than highway results.

sources.citation: Shao, G., Hightower, J., & Schindel, W. (2023). Credibility consideration for digital twins in manufacturing. Manufacturing Letters, 35, 24-28. Online December 2022.
sources.question: What makes twin outputs credible for decisions?
sources.method: Discusses verification, validation, uncertainty and extension of a twin framework standard.
sources.evaluation: No numerical efficacy claim made from abstract.
sources.supported_finding: VVUQ belongs throughout the twin lifecycle; credibility also includes other factors.
sources.limitations: Manufacturing scope; framework discussion is not empirical proof of a particular highway model.
sources.reproducibility_access: NIST abstract and publication-year reconciliation verified; linked PDF fetch failed.
sources.reading_depth: Institutional abstract and citation metadata only
sources.relevance: Separate software correctness, real-world agreement and uncertainty.

sources.citation: Dembski, F., Wössner, U., Letzgus, M., Ruddat, M., & Yamu, C. (2020). Urban Digital Twins for Smart Cities and Citizens: The Case Study of Herrenberg, Germany. Sustainability, 12(6), 2307.
sources.question: Can urban models and simulation support participatory planning?
sources.method: Combines city geometry, space syntax, SUMO, OpenFOAM, sensors and COVISE/OpenCOVER immersive visualization.
sources.data: Herrenberg city and environmental data; citizen observations; 39 survey respondents aged 16-80.
sources.evaluation: Nine-question survey, polarity profiles and open answers; Fig.8 compares prior-participation groups.
sources.supported_finding: Demonstrates integrated urban visualization with broadly positive participant judgments.
sources.limitations: Small nonrepresentative sample; no randomized interface comparator; positive opinions do not validate traffic or pollution prediction.
sources.reproducibility_access: CC BY publisher PDF retained; software named/public COVISE link, but end-to-end datasets and replay not established.
sources.reading_depth: Deep anchor: section 3 components pp.4-8 and sections 4.3-5 pp.12-15; Fig.8 visually inspected (PDF page14).
sources.relevance: Direct prior art for combining SUMO, urban models and immersive participation; integration alone is not a novelty claim.

sources.citation: Ketzler, B., Naserentin, V., Latino, F., Zangelidis, C., Thuvander, L., & Logg, A. (2020). Digital Twins for Cities: A State of the Art Review. Built Environment, 46(4), 547-573.
sources.question: How do urban twins relate to 3D city models?
sources.method: Academic terminology review and practical examples from grey literature.
sources.evaluation: Concept/application comparison, not an accuracy benchmark.
sources.supported_finding: Urban usage extends beyond geometry to semantic, sensor and simulation information; no consensus definition reported.
sources.limitations: Historical review and grey-literature examples do not independently validate deployment claims.
sources.reproducibility_access: Institutional abstract/metadata accessible; full text not read.
sources.relevance: Broadens the foundation beyond traffic control.

sources.citation: Slater, M., Banakou, D., Beacco, A., Gallego, J., Macia-Varela, F., & Oliva, R. (2022). A Separate Reality: An Update on Place Illusion and Plausibility in Virtual Reality. Frontiers in Virtual Reality, 3, 914392.
sources.question: How should presence and plausibility be understood and measured?
sources.method: Reviews competing constructs and measurement approaches.
sources.data: Prior studies; no new single benchmark dataset.
sources.evaluation: Table 1 compares questionnaires, behavior/physiology, breaks, configuration transitions and sentiment methods.
sources.supported_finding: Separates system affordances from subjective response and recommends triangulating measures.
sources.limitations: A theoretical position with contested terminology; cited experiments were not all independently read.
sources.reproducibility_access: Open full HTML; no new experiment to reproduce.
sources.reading_depth: Deep anchor: Place Illusion and Plausibility, Coherence, Measurement and Table1; targeted full-text reading.
sources.relevance: XR usefulness and perceived realism need task-specific measurement, separate from simulation validity.

sources.citation: Latoschik, M. E., & Wienrich, C. (2022). Congruence and Plausibility, Not Presence: Pivotal Conditions for XR Experiences and Effects, a Novel Approach. Frontiers in Virtual Reality, 3, 694433.
sources.question: Can a framework cover VR, AR and MR more broadly than place illusion?
sources.method: Conceptual critique and proposed congruence/plausibility model.
sources.data: No new experiment in this perspective.
sources.supported_finding: Offers a competing account of XR experience, explicitly challenging presence-centered framing.
sources.limitations: Proposal is not established superiority; terminology differs from T08.
sources.reading_depth: Targeted introduction and discussion of current presence-oriented theories
sources.relevance: Avoid treating one XR taxonomy as universally accepted.

sources.citation: Hofer, M., Hartmann, T., Eden, A., Ratan, R., & Hahn, L. (2020). The Role of Plausibility in the Experience of Spatial Presence in Virtual Environments. Frontiers in Virtual Reality, 1, 2.
sources.question: Do external plausibility violations reduce spatial presence?
sources.method: Randomized 2x2x2 between-subject design: plausibility, HMD/monitor immersion, cognitive load.
sources.evaluation: SPES self-location/possible-action scales; ANOVA and one-tailed equivalence tests using delta=0.15.
sources.supported_finding: HMD condition increased presence; plausibility manipulation changed perceived plausibility but did not reduce presence under tested conditions.
sources.limitations: House exploration/student sample; one kind of inconsistency; possible-actions residual normality issue; no highway decision or transfer measure.
sources.reproducibility_access: Open HTML methods; no independently verified runnable artifact.
sources.reading_depth: Deep anchor: Current Study, Method, Measures, Results and Discussion full sections.
sources.relevance: Empirical warning against using subjective presence as a proxy for physical realism or predictive truth.

sources.citation: Grübel, J., Thrash, T., Aguilar, L., Gath-Morad, M., Chatain, J., Sumner, R. W., Hölscher, C., & Schinazi, V. R. (2022). The Hitchhiker's Guide to Fused Twins: A Review of Access to Digital Twins in situ in Smart Cities. Remote Sensing, 14(13), 3095.
sources.type: Review with journal DOI; author-deposited preprint abstract accessed
sources.question: How can situated analytics connect urban data to its physical location?
sources.method: Reviews twins, situated analytics and smart cities; proposes fused-twin framing.
sources.evaluation: No new comparative effect size established by accessed abstract.
sources.supported_finding: Connects physical, data, analytical, virtual and connection environments to in-situ access.
sources.limitations: Conceptual potential is not evidence that AR improves every decision; full methods not read.
sources.reproducibility_access: arXiv v2 dated 2022-06-08; publisher fetch failed.
sources.relevance: XR as spatially situated access, beyond a desktop or immersive replica.

sources.citation: Lei, B., Janssen, P., Stoter, J., & Biljecki, F. (2023). Challenges of urban digital twins: A systematic review and a Delphi expert survey. Automation in Construction, 147, 104716.
sources.type: Peer-reviewed systematic review and expert survey
sources.question: Which technical and nontechnical obstacles affect urban twins?
sources.method: Literature review plus three-round Delphi survey.
sources.data: 34 reviewed papers; expert panel (count not independently checked here).
sources.evaluation: Expert issue-severity ratings on five-point scale; synthesis mapped to lifecycle.
sources.supported_finding: Combined taxonomy includes 14 technical and 9 nontechnical challenges; social/legal/practical-value concerns supplement data and interoperability problems.
sources.limitations: Expert judgment and historical corpus; severity is not causal evidence or a ranking for this team.
sources.reproducibility_access: Publisher indexed methods/results inspected; institutional metadata confirms citation; repository PDF fetch timed out.
sources.reading_depth: Targeted publisher text: Delphi design, Results, Discussion, Conclusion; not counted as deep anchor
sources.relevance: Scope, purpose, governance and data maintenance belong in feasibility, not only rendering technology.
